- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. - sprite: Use this skill when users are modifying system configuration, starting dev servers, requesting services (databases, Docker, Redis, etc.), installing dependencies or runtimes, or when they have made a functional change to their code that appears to be working (to create a checkpoint). Also use for managing checkpoints, restores, and understanding network policy in the Sprite VM.
- sprite-api-gateway: Use this skill when users want to access external APIs (GitHub, Slack, Linear, etc.), integrate with third-party services, or need authenticated API calls. The API gateway at api.sprites.dev handles authentication automatically — sprites never need raw API keys or tokens.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.

content.content:
# Sprites Manager

Run **Claude Code inside a [Fly.io Sprite](https://sprites.dev)** (a cloud dev VM) and
drive it from your phone. Set up a sprite once on your computer, then start, watch, and guide
coding sessions from anywhere — close the app and pick the same session back up later.

> Personal project against the new Sprites API. Focused on Claude Code today; other agents later.

---

## Quick start (the workflow this app is built around)

The smoothest setup is to prepare a sprite on your computer, then connect from the phone:

1. **Create a sprite** — tap **+** on the dashboard, or use the Sprites CLI on your computer.
2. **Add an SSH key** so the sprite can reach GitHub. In a sprite shell:
   ```bash
   ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "you@example.com"
   cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub        # add this to GitHub → Settings → SSH and GPG keys
   ```
3. **Clone your repo** into the sprite:
   ```bash
   git clone git@github.com:you/your-repo.git ~/your-repo
   ```
4. **Connect from the phone.** Open the sprite, set the session **working directory** to your
   repo (e.g. `/home/sprite/your-repo`), type a prompt, and send. Claude starts working with no
   approval prompts.
5. **Come back anytime.** Reopen the app and you land in the same session — send another message
   to continue the conversation.

The same flow is available in-app under **Guides** (dashboard → Guides).

---

## Connecting: Chat, sessions, and terminals

The default is **Chat**; the terminals and the session browser are reached from a sprite's
**Overview → "Sessions & terminals"** (the browser is also on the 🕓 clock in the chat header).

| | What it is | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| **Chat** (default) | Runs Claude non-interactively (`claude -p --output-format stream-json`) as a one-shot Sprites *service* and streams the result into a native chat with tool/plan/result cards. | Day-to-day prompting and reading results comfortably on a phone. |
| **Session browser** | Reads Claude's own transcripts (`~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl`) off the sprite, lists every past session with a preview, renders its full history natively, and **Continues** it via `--resume <id>`. The same data `claude --resume` shows on a computer. | Picking up any past session — even on a fresh install, since history lives on the sprite, not the phone. |
| **Stream terminal** | A real TTY over a WebSocket (`/v1/sprites/{name}/exec`) rendered in a Skia terminal. Auto-runs `cd <repo> && claude`; run anything, including `claude --resume`. | Answering Claude's interactive prompts, watching the live TUI, full shell control. |
| **Web Terminal (ttyd)** · *legacy* | Embeds a [`ttyd`](https://github.com/tsl0922/ttyd) web terminal running *inside* the sprite, via a WebView. Superseded by the above. | Reference / a full xterm in a WebView. Requires starting ttyd in the sprite. |

A chat you reopen also auto-syncs from its transcript, so turns that completed (or were started from
a terminal) while the app was closed show up when you come back.

### Dictation and audio transcription

The chat input has three experimental audio paths:

- **Mic** uses device speech recognition and streams interim text into the input while you speak.
  It does not send the message automatically.
- **Rec** records audio on the phone, then transcribes it with the selected **Transcribe** backend.
- **File** lets you pick an audio file, then transcribes it with the selected **Transcribe** backend.

`Rec` and `File` can use one of three backends:

- **Sprite** uploads the audio to the sprite and runs a local backend there. Install one inside the
  sprite, for example `pip install -U faster-whisper` or `pipx install openai-whisper`.
- **Assembly** uploads directly from the client to AssemblyAI. Save an AssemblyAI API key under
  **Settings → Transcription** first.
- **OpenAI** uploads directly from the client to OpenAI's transcription API. Save an OpenAI API key
  under **Settings → Transcription** first.

Transcripts are appended to the input box for review/editing; tap send yourself when it looks right.

### Session working directory

Claude is always launched after `cd`-ing into the session's **working directory**. This matters
twice over:

- It's where your cloned repo lives, so set it per session (or set a default in Settings).
- Claude keys its **resumable history by directory**, so resuming only works from the same path.
  The working directory is therefore locked once a conversation starts — begin a new session to
  switch folders.

If your repo lives at `~/type/type_new`, use `/home/sprite/type/type_new` in the app. `~` resolves

46	
47	- **Not Expo Go.** The app bundles custom native modules (`@shopify/react-native-skia`,
48	  `react-native-webview`, `react-native-reanimated`/`worklets`). It requires a

50	  dependency add/update or `app.json` native-config change, rebuild with
51	  `npx expo prebuild --clean && npx expo run:ios`. JS/TSX-only changes hot-reload.
52	- **`.npmrc` with `legacy-peer-deps=true` is committed and load-bearing.** A web

54	  error out. EAS cloud builds also read this file. Do not remove it.
55	- **`metro.config.js` contains two non-obvious hacks** — don't "simplify" it:
56	  1. Maps `punycode` to the real npm package (RN polyfill isn't enough for some deps).

58	     v7.28+'s package exports map omits `.js` but the helpers require with `.js`,
59	     which Metro can't match. The custom `resolveRequest` fixes this.
60	- **No tests.** There is no test runner configured. `scripts/test-ws-server.js`
61	  is a *manual* dummy server for terminal development, not an automated test.
62	  Don't claim to "run tests" — run `npm run lint` instead.
63	- **Bundle identifier inconsistency in the repo:** `app.json` uses
64	  `com.digital.spritespack` (both `ios.bundleIdentifier` and `android.package`),
65	  but `README.md`/`DEPLOYMENT.md` reference `com.digital.spritesmanager`. Treat
66	  `app.json` as the source of truth. Change the id in one place if you need to
67	  rekey the app.
68	- **EAS versioning:** `eas.json` sets `cli.appVersionSource: "remote"` and
69	  `production.autoIncrement: true`. EAS bumps the **build number** automatically;
70	  bump `expo.version` in `app.json` only for a new marketing release. Don't also
71	  hand-bump `ios.buildNumber`.
72	- **React Compiler is ON** (`app.json` → `experiments.reactCompiler: true`),
73	  and `typedRoutes: true`. Keep components compiler-friendly (no unstable
74	  hook closures returning new objects on every render where avoidable).
75	
76	## Architecture
77	
78	### Route layout (Expo Router, file-based, `src/app/`)
79	
80	```
81	_layout.tsx        Root: ThemeProvider (light/dark) + AuthProvider, Stack
82	index.tsx          Loading/redirect based on auth state
83	auth.tsx           3-step sign-in (Sprites token → Claude token → GitHub)
84	api/[...path]+api.ts   Web-only reverse proxy to api.sprites.dev (see below)
85	(app)/             Auth-gated group (redirects to /auth if not signed in)
86	  _layout.tsx      Authenticated Stack
87	  index.tsx        Dashboard — sprite list, create sprite, links to Guides/Settings
88	  guide.tsx        In-app setup walkthrough
89	  settings.tsx     Defaults: provider, claude model, max turns, instructions,
90	                   working directory, git name/email, transcription keys,
91	                   auto-checkpoint
92	  sprite/[name].tsx  The main screen: tabs Overview / Chat / Checkpoints,
93	                     plus session browser + terminals entry points
94	  exec-poc.tsx     Stream terminal (WebSocket exec → Skia terminal)
95	  ttyd-terminal.tsx  Legacy web terminal (ttyd in a WebView)
96	```
97	
98	### The chat streaming pipeline (the core of the app)
99	
100	`src/hooks/useChat.ts` is the single hook that drives chat. Flow:
101	
102	1. On send, it builds a shell command: `mkdir -p <wd> && cd <wd> && git config ... &&
103	   export CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=... && export NO_DNA=1 && claude -p --verbose
104	   --output-format stream-json --dangerously-skip-permissions --model <m>
105	   [--max-turns N] [--append-system-prompt '...'] [--resume <id>] '<prompt>'`.
106	   The whole thing is wrapped in a **heartbeat subshell**
107	   `{ (while true; do sleep 20; printf . >&2; done) & HBEAT=$!; trap "kill $HBEAT" EXIT; <cmd>; kill $HBEAT; }`
108	   to keep the Sprites service log stream alive.
109	2. It starts a Sprites **service** via `api.streamService()` (`PUT /sprites/{name}/services/{svc}`)
110	   with `cmd: 'bash', args: ['-c', fullCommand]`. Output streams back as NDJSON.
111	3. Each service log line is `ServiceLogEvent` (`{type:'stdout'|'stderr'|'exit'|..., data}`).
112	   The `data` of a `stdout` line is itself a line of Claude's `stream-json` NDJSON,
113	   prefixed by a log timestamp like `2026-02-19T09:13:24.665Z [stdout] `.
114	   `stripLogTimestamps()` strips that prefix; `ClaudeStreamParser` parses the inner NDJSON.
115	   This is a **two-level NDJSON** parse — easy to miss.
116	4. Parsed `ClaudeStreamEvent`s (`system`/`assistant`/`user`(tool_result)/`result`)
117	   are applied to the in-memory `ChatMessage[]` via `updateActiveAssistant`. Tool-use
118	   blocks become `ToolUseCard`s; matching tool_results attach the `result` back to the
119	   card and also push a `toolResult` content item.
120	5. `processedUUIDsRef` dedupes Claude events by `uuid`, because service-log replay can
121	   re-emit lines.
122	6. If `streamService` returns zero events, it falls back to `streamServiceLogs` (replay).
123	7. On reopen, if the chat has a `claudeSessionId`, `loadSession` pulls the on-disk
124	   transcript (`readClaudeSessionMessages`) and `mergeTranscript` overlays it,
125	   **preserving message ids for the shared prefix** so React reuses bubbles instead
126	   of remounting/re-scrolling. `conversationSignature` short-circuits the setState if
127	   nothing actually changed (this was a real bug: reopening looked like the last turn
128	   was duplicated and re-answered).
129	
130	### Codex provider
131	
132	`AgentProvider = 'claude' | 'codex' | 'codexAppServer'`. The chat layer is
133	provider-abstracted. The two Codex providers intentionally expose the two
134	transport paths side-by-side:
135	
136	- `codex`: legacy/fallback `codex exec --json` / `codex exec resume --json
137	  <id>`, still parsed by `CodexStreamParser` / `parseCodexEvent`.
138	- `codexAppServer`: `codex app-server --stdio`; `useChat` drives the
139	  JSON-RPC handshake through `streamCodexAppServerTurn`
140	  (`initialize` → `thread/start`/`thread/resume` → `turn/start`), with stdin
141	  carried over the Exec WebSocket.
142	
143	Both modes use `--skip-git-repo-check` and/or no-approval/full-access settings
144	where the CLI supports them. Codex auth issues are sniffed from stderr by
145	`classifyCodexAuthIssue` (looks for `codex login`, 401/403, etc.) and surfaced
146	with a switch-to-Claude prompt. Codex is keyed on `codexSessionId` (Codex thread
147	id); Claude on `claudeSessionId`.
148	
149	### Session browser (`src/services/claude-sessions.ts`)
150	
151	Reads Claude's own on-disk transcripts from the sprite — the same data
152	`claude --resume` shows. Claude stores one JSONL per session under
153	`~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/<session-id>.jsonl`. `listClaudeSessions`
154	runs a small Node script on the sprite (via `runExec`) that scans every
155	transcript and emits a compact JSON summary wrapped in `@@WISP@@…@@WISP@@`
156	sentinel markers (extracted by `extractSentinel` to tolerate shell noise).
157	`transcriptToMessages` converts a raw transcript into the app's `ChatMessage[]`
158	so the existing chat UI renders it natively.
159	
160	### Dictation and audio transcription
161	
162	`src/hooks/useChatDictation.ts` owns the chat input's audio paths:
163	
164	- `Mic` uses `expo-speech-recognition` directly on the device with interim
165	  results enabled. It streams text into the input box as the user speaks.
166	- `Rec` uses `expo-audio` to record locally, then transcribes the recording.
167	- `File` uses `expo-document-picker` to select an audio file, then transcribes
168	  the file.
169	
170	`Rec` and `File` route through the persisted `transcriptionProvider` setting:
171	
172	- `sprite` (default): `src/services/audio-transcription.ts` uploads to the
173	  sprite and runs a local backend (`whisper`, Python `whisper`, or
174	  `faster_whisper`). This needs a backend installed inside each target sprite.
175	- `assemblyai`: `src/services/client-transcription.ts` uploads directly from
176	  the client to AssemblyAI, creates a transcript, and polls it. The request sets
177	  language detection with expected languages `en` and `ru`.
178	- `openai`: `src/services/client-transcription.ts` uploads directly from the
179	  client to OpenAI's `/v1/audio/transcriptions` endpoint with
180	  `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`.
181	
182	All transcription paths append text to the chat input only; they do **not**
183	auto-send the chat message. AssemblyAI and OpenAI keys are stored via
184	`src/services/auth.ts` (`assemblyAiToken`, `openAiToken`) and configured in
185	Settings → Transcription.
186	
187	### Terminal (`src/components/terminal/`)
188	
189	A from-scratch Skia terminal (not xterm.js): `AnsiParser` → `TerminalBuffer`
190	(port of xterm.js's Buffer + InputHandler, with the 256-color palette) →
191	`SkiaTerminalRenderer` (Skia draw) → `SkiaTerminal` (gestures, keyboard,
192	selection, reconnect). Input goes over a WebSocket to
193	`/v1/sprites/{name}/exec` (`src/services/exec-poc.ts`). `TerminalErrorBoundary`
194	wraps it. On web, Skia loads via CanvasKit (`components/web/WithSkiaWeb.tsx`)
195	and `exec-poc.tsx` `require()`s the native component conditionally.
196	
197	### Auth & storage
198	
199	- **Tokens** (`src/services/auth.ts`): `expo-secure-store` on native, `localStorage`
200	  on web. Three keys: `spritesToken` (Sprites API), `claudeToken`
201	  (`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, injected at launch time), `githubToken` (device flow,
202	  optional — used to auto-fill git name/email), plus optional `assemblyAiToken`
203	  and `openAiToken` for client-side audio transcription. `AuthContext` exposes state.
204	- **Chats & settings** (`src/services/storage.ts`): AsyncStorage with prefixes
205	  `sprite_chats_<spriteName>` (the list of `PersistedChat`), `chat_meta_<chatId>`
206	  (the `ChatMessage[]`), `setting_<key>` (string settings) / `setting_<key>`=`'true'|'false'`
207	  for bools. `normalizePersistedChat` defensively sanitizes on load and re-saves
208	  if the shape changed (migration).
209	
210	### API layer (`src/services/api.ts`)
211	
212	REST client for `api.sprites.dev/v1` (Sprites: list/create/delete, checkpoints,
213	services, exec). `BASE_URL` is **platform-conditional**:
214	`Platform.OS === 'web' ? '/api/v1' : 'https://api.sprites.dev/v1'`. On web, the
215	Expo Router route `src/app/api/[...path]+api.ts` proxies all `/api/*` requests to
216	`https://api.sprites.dev` (browsers can't carry the bearer token cross-origin).
217	`runExec` is a helper that runs a one-shot `bash -c '<cmd>'` as a temporary
218	service, collects stdout, and cleans up — used by the session browser and
219	sprite wake-up. `startBackgroundService` fires a service without awaiting and
220	resolves once the first lifecycle event arrives.
221	
222	### `remote-agent/` (separate Node daemon)
223	
224	A standalone daemon (`node-pty` + `ws`) that implements the *exact same* Sprites
225	wire protocol (`/sprites/:name/services/:svc`, `/sprites/:name/exec`, etc.) so
226	the app can connect to **any Linux machine**, not just Sprites. The `:name`
227	segment is ignored. Install with `bash remote-agent/install.sh` (generates an
228	`AGENT_TOKEN`, writes a systemd user service on port 8765). See
229	`remote-agent/MIGRATION.md` for the planned app change: base URLs and token
230	source become per-connection instead of global. **When that migration lands,
231	update this doc.**
232	
233	## Non-obvious conventions & invariants
234	
235	- **Working directory is locked per chat once a conversation starts.** Claude
236	  keys resumable history by cwd (`~/.claude/projects/<hashed-cwd>/`), so
237	  `--resume <id>` only works from the same path. Helpers in
238	  `src/constants/session.ts`: `DEFAULT_WORKING_DIRECTORY = '/home/sprite/project'`,
239	  `normalizeWorkingDirectory`, `shortWorkingDirectory`. `~` expands to
240	  `/home/sprite` on the sprite — always use absolute paths in the app.
241	- **`--dangerously-skip-permissions` (Claude) / `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` (Codex)
242	  are always passed.** No approval prompts — autonomous coding is the point.
243	  Safety net is the Checkpoints tab (snapshot/restore the filesystem).
244	- **One `useChat` instance is shared across all chats in a sprite.** Switching
245	  sessions calls `chat.interrupt()` first to stop any in-flight stream, then
246	  swaps `chatId`/`workingDirectory`/session ids. Don't instantiate per-session.
247	- **Service names are random** (`wisp-<provider>-<id>` via `makeServiceName`),
248	  so each send is a fresh service. `interrupt()` aborts the stream and
249	  `deleteService()`s the current one.
250	- **Path aliases** (`tsconfig.json`): `@/*` → `./src/*`, `@/assets/*` → `./assets/*`.
251	- **Theming:** `useTheme()` (`src/hooks/use-theme.ts`) returns the active
252	  `Colors` palette from `src/constants/theme.ts` (light/dark aware via
253	  `useColorScheme`). Use `Spacing`/`FontSize` constants, not magic numbers.
254	  `BottomTabInset` and `MaxContentWidth` are defined there too.
255	- **Ids:** `makeId()` in `src/models/chat.ts` (`Math.random().toString(36) + Date.now().toString(36)`).
256	- **Section comments:** `api.ts` uses `// MARK: - <Section>` (Objective-C style).
257	- **Debug logging** is `__DEV__`-gated (e.g. `debugChat`). Don't leave console
258	  logs that run in production.
259	- **`NO_DNA=1`** is exported before launching Claude (internal flag). Keep it.
260	- **`expo-splash-screen`, `expo-router`, `expo-secure-store`** are the configured
261	  plugins in `app.json`. iOS export compliance is pre-declared
262	  (`ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption: false`).
263	- **Generated native folders (`/ios`, `/android`) are gitignored.** They're
264	  produced by `expo prebuild` (run automatically by `expo run:ios`/`run:android`).
265	
266	## When you change things
267	
268	- **Adding a native dependency or native config** → rebuild
269	  (`npx expo prebuild --clean && npx expo run:ios`). JS-only edits hot-reload.
270	- **Adding a new screen** → put it under `src/app/(app)/` and register a
271	  `Stack.Screen` in `src/app/(app)/_layout.tsx`. Auth-gated routes go inside
272	  the `(app)` group.
273	- **Adding a new service API call** → add to `src/services/api.ts`, follow the
274	  `apiRequest`/`AppError` pattern. For streaming endpoints, mirror
275	  `streamService` (NDJSON line buffer + `parseServiceEventLine`).
276	- **Adding a new Claude event shape** → extend `src/models/claude-events.ts`
277	  (`ClaudeContentBlock`, `parseClaudeEvent`) and handle it in
278	  `useChat.handleClaudeEvent`.
279	- **Touching `useChat`** → it's large and ref-heavy. Read the whole file first.
280	  The refs (`messagesRef`, `activeUser/AssistantMessageIdRef`,
281	  `toolUseIndexRef`, `processedUUIDsRef`, `loadRequestRef`) are the source of
282	  truth inside callbacks; `useState` mirrors them for render. Don't split
283	  without preserving the ref-mirror invariant.
284	- **Touching the terminal** → `TerminalBuffer` is a faithful xterm.js port;
285	  preserve its semantics. Test with `scripts/test-ws-server.js` against a real
286	  `claude` TUI.
287	
288	## Further reading
289	
290	- `README.md` — user-facing workflow and the three connection modes (chat,
291	  session browser, stream terminal, ttyd).
292	- `DEPLOYMENT.md` — iOS simulator/device/TestFlight/EAS deep dive.
293	- `remote-agent/MIGRATION.md` — plan for per-connection base URLs (remote machines).

   to keep the Sprites service log stream alive.
2. It starts a Sprites **service** via `api.streamService()` (`PUT /sprites/{name}/services/{svc}`)
   with `cmd: 'bash', args: ['-c', fullCommand]`. Output streams back as NDJSON.
3. Each service log line is `ServiceLogEvent` (`{type:'stdout'|'stderr'|'exit'|..., data}`).
   The `data` of a `stdout` line is itself a line of Claude's `stream-json` NDJSON,
   prefixed by a log timestamp like `2026-02-19T09:13:24.665Z [stdout] `.
   `stripLogTimestamps()` strips that prefix; `ClaudeStreamParser` parses the inner NDJSON.
   This is a **two-level NDJSON** parse — easy to miss.
4. Parsed `ClaudeStreamEvent`s (`system`/`assistant`/`user`(tool_result)/`result`)
   are applied to the in-memory `ChatMessage[]` via `updateActiveAssistant`. Tool-use
   blocks become `ToolUseCard`s; matching tool_results attach the `result` back to the
   card and also push a `toolResult` content item.
5. `processedUUIDsRef` dedupes Claude events by `uuid`, because service-log replay can
   re-emit lines.
6. If `streamService` returns zero events, it falls back to `streamServiceLogs` (replay).
7. On reopen, if the chat has a `claudeSessionId`, `loadSession` pulls the on-disk
   transcript (`readClaudeSessionMessages`) and `mergeTranscript` overlays it,
   **preserving message ids for the shared prefix** so React reuses bubbles instead
   of remounting/re-scrolling. `conversationSignature` short-circuits the setState if
   nothing actually changed (this was a real bug: reopening looked like the last turn
   was duplicated and re-answered).

### Codex provider

`AgentProvider = 'claude' | 'codex' | 'codexAppServer'`. The chat layer is
provider-abstracted. The two Codex providers intentionally expose the two
transport paths side-by-side:

- `codex`: legacy/fallback `codex exec --json` / `codex exec resume --json
  <id>`, still parsed by `CodexStreamParser` / `parseCodexEvent`.
- `codexAppServer`: `codex app-server --stdio`; `useChat` drives the
  JSON-RPC handshake through `streamCodexAppServerTurn`
  (`initialize` → `thread/start`/`thread/resume` → `turn/start`), with stdin
  carried over the Exec WebSocket.

Both modes use `--skip-git-repo-check` and/or no-approval/full-access settings
where the CLI supports them. Codex auth issues are sniffed from stderr by
`classifyCodexAuthIssue` (looks for `codex login`, 401/403, etc.) and surfaced
with a switch-to-Claude prompt. Codex is keyed on `codexSessionId` (Codex thread
id); Claude on `claudeSessionId`.

### Session browser (`src/services/claude-sessions.ts`)

Reads Claude's own on-disk transcripts from the sprite — the same data
`claude --resume` shows. Claude stores one JSONL per session under
`~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/<session-id>.jsonl`. `listClaudeSessions`
runs a small Node script on the sprite (via `runExec`) that scans every
transcript and emits a compact JSON summary wrapped in `@@WISP@@…@@WISP@@`
sentinel markers (extracted by `extractSentinel` to tolerate shell noise).
`transcriptToMessages` converts a raw transcript into the app's `ChatMessage[]`
so the existing chat UI renders it natively.

### Dictation and audio transcription

`src/hooks/useChatDictation.ts` owns the chat input's audio paths:

- `Mic` uses `expo-speech-recognition` directly on the device with interim
  results enabled. It streams text into the input box as the user speaks.
- `Rec` uses `expo-audio` to record locally, then transcribes the recording.
- `File` uses `expo-document-picker` to select an audio file, then transcribes
  the file.

`Rec` and `File` route through the persisted `transcriptionProvider` setting:

- `sprite` (default): `src/services/audio-transcription.ts` uploads to the
  sprite and runs a local backend (`whisper`, Python `whisper`, or
  `faster_whisper`). This needs a backend installed inside each target sprite.
- `assemblyai`: `src/services/client-transcription.ts` uploads directly from
  the client to AssemblyAI, creates a transcript, and polls it. The request sets
  language detection with expected languages `en` and `ru`.
- `openai`: `src/services/client-transcription.ts` uploads directly from the
  client to OpenAI's `/v1/audio/transcriptions` endpoint with
  `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`.

All transcription paths append text to the chat input only; they do **not**
auto-send the chat message. AssemblyAI and OpenAI keys are stored via
`src/services/auth.ts` (`assemblyAiToken`, `openAiToken`) and configured in
Settings → Transcription.

### Terminal (`src/components/terminal/`)

A from-scratch Skia terminal (not xterm.js): `AnsiParser` → `TerminalBuffer`
(port of xterm.js's Buffer + InputHandler, with the 256-color palette) →
`SkiaTerminalRenderer` (Skia draw) → `SkiaTerminal` (gestures, keyboard,
selection, reconnect). Input goes over a WebSocket to
`/v1/sprites/{name}/exec` (`src/services/exec-poc.ts`). `TerminalErrorBoundary`
wraps it. On web, Skia loads via CanvasKit (`components/web/WithSkiaWeb.tsx`)
and `exec-poc.tsx` `require()`s the native component conditionally.

### Auth & storage

- **Tokens** (`src/services/auth.ts`): `expo-secure-store` on native, `localStorage`
  on web. Three keys: `spritesToken` (Sprites API), `claudeToken`
  (`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, injected at launch time), `githubToken` (device flow,
  optional — used to auto-fill git name/email), plus optional `assemblyAiToken`
  and `openAiToken` for client-side audio transcription. `AuthContext` exposes state.
- **Chats & settings** (`src/services/storage.ts`): AsyncStorage with prefixes
  `sprite_chats_<spriteName>` (the list of `PersistedChat`), `chat_meta_<chatId>`
  (the `ChatMessage[]`), `setting_<key>` (string settings) / `setting_<key>`=`'true'|'false'`
  for bools. `normalizePersistedChat` defensively sanitizes on load and re-saves
  if the shape changed (migration).

### API layer (`src/services/api.ts`)

REST client for `api.sprites.dev/v1` (Sprites: list/create/delete, checkpoints,
services, exec). `BASE_URL` is **platform-conditional**:
`Platform.OS === 'web' ? '/api/v1' : 'https://api.sprites.dev/v1'`. On web, the
Expo Router route `src/app/api/[...path]+api.ts` proxies all `/api/*` requests to
`https://api.sprites.dev` (browsers can't carry the bearer token cross-origin).
`runExec` is a helper that runs a one-shot `bash -c '<cmd>'` as a temporary
service, collects stdout, and cleans up — used by the session browser and
sprite wake-up. `startBackgroundService` fires a service without awaiting and
resolves once the first lifecycle event arrives.

### `remote-agent/` (separate Node daemon)

A standalone daemon (`node-pty` + `ws`) that implements the *exact same* Sprites
wire protocol (`/sprites/:name/services/:svc`, `/sprites/:name/exec`, etc.) so
the app can connect to **any Linux machine**, not just Sprites. The `:name`
segment is ignored. Install with `bash remote-agent/install.sh` (generates an
`AGENT_TOKEN`, writes a systemd user service on port 8765). See
`remote-agent/MIGRATION.md` for the planned app change: base URLs and token
source become per-connection instead of global. **When that migration lands,
update this doc.**

## Non-obvious conventions & invariants

- **Working directory is locked per chat once a conversation starts.** Claude
  keys resumable history by cwd (`~/.claude/projects/<hashed-cwd>/`), so
  `--resume <id>` only works from the same path. Helpers in
  `src/constants/session.ts`: `DEFAULT_WORKING_DIRECTORY = '/home/sprite/project'`,
  `normalizeWorkingDirectory`, `shortWorkingDirectory`. `~` expands to
  `/home/sprite` on the sprite — always use absolute paths in the app.
- **`--dangerously-skip-permissions` (Claude) / `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` (Codex)
  are always passed.** No approval prompts — autonomous coding is the point.
  Safety net is the Checkpoints tab (snapshot/restore the filesystem).
- **One `useChat` instance is shared across all chats in a sprite.** Switching
  sessions calls `chat.interrupt()` first to stop any in-flight stream, then
  swaps `chatId`/`workingDirectory`/session ids. Don't instantiate per-session.
- **Service names are random** (`wisp-<provider>-<id>` via `makeServiceName`),
  so each send is a fresh service. `interrupt()` aborts the stream and
  `deleteService()`s the current one.
- **Path aliases** (`tsconfig.json`): `@/*` → `./src/*`, `@/assets/*` → `./assets/*`.
- **Theming:** `useTheme()` (`src/hooks/use-theme.ts`) returns the active
  `Colors` palette from `src/constants/theme.ts` (light/dark aware via
  `useColorScheme`). Use `Spacing`/`FontSize` constants, not magic numbers.
  `BottomTabInset` and `MaxContentWidth` are defined there too.
- **Ids:** `makeId()` in `src/models/chat.ts` (`Math.random().toString(36) + Date.now().toString(36)`).
- **Section comments:** `api.ts` uses `// MARK: - <Section>` (Objective-C style).
- **Debug logging** is `__DEV__`-gated (e.g. `debugChat`). Don't leave console
  logs that run in production.
- **`NO_DNA=1`** is exported before launching Claude (internal flag). Keep it.
- **`expo-splash-screen`, `expo-router`, `expo-secure-store`** are the configured
  plugins in `app.json`. iOS export compliance is pre-declared
  (`ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption: false`).
- **Generated native folders (`/ios`, `/android`) are gitignored.** They're
  produced by `expo prebuild` (run automatically by `expo run:ios`/`run:android`).

## When you change things

- **Adding a native dependency or native config** → rebuild
  (`npx expo prebuild --clean && npx expo run:ios`). JS-only edits hot-reload.
- **Adding a new screen** → put it under `src/app/(app)/` and register a
  `Stack.Screen` in `src/app/(app)/_layout.tsx`. Auth-gated routes go inside
  the `(app)` group.
- **Adding a new service API call** → add to `src/services/api.ts`, follow the
  `apiRequest`/`AppError` pattern. For streaming endpoints, mirror
  `streamService` (NDJSON line buffer + `parseServiceEventLine`).
- **Adding a new Claude event shape** → extend `src/models/claude-events.ts`
  (`ClaudeContentBlock`, `parseClaudeEvent`) and handle it in
  `useChat.handleClaudeEvent`.
- **Touching `useChat`** → it's large and ref-heavy. Read the whole file first.
  The refs (`messagesRef`, `activeUser/AssistantMessageIdRef`,
  `toolUseIndexRef`, `processedUUIDsRef`, `loadRequestRef`) are the source of
  truth inside callbacks; `useState` mirrors them for render. Don't split
  without preserving the ref-mirror invariant.
- **Touching the terminal** → `TerminalBuffer` is a faithful xterm.js port;
  preserve its semantics. Test with `scripts/test-ws-server.js` against a real
  `claude` TUI.

## Further reading

- `README.md` — user-facing workflow and the three connection modes (chat,
  session browser, stream terminal, ttyd).
- `DEPLOYMENT.md` — iOS simulator/device/TestFlight/EAS deep dive.
- `remote-agent/MIGRATION.md` — plan for per-connection base URLs (remote machines).

# TODO

## Credential provisioning follow-ups

### 1. Verify the captured `claude login` credentials replay
The "Log in with browser" → Capture flow stores `~/.claude/.credentials.json` from a
sprite and replays it onto new sprites via `buildProvisionCommand` (the `claudeCreds`
branch). This path is **not yet verified on a real sprite** — Claude Code reading a
replayed credentials file (and refreshing the access token via the embedded refresh
token) is the part most likely to break across CLI versions.

- Smoke-test on one sprite: capture a login, create a fresh sprite, confirm Claude runs
  authed and keeps working past the access-token expiry (refresh works).
- Safe default meanwhile: the pasted-token path (`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` written to
  `~/.sprite_env`) is well-trodden and stays the fallback.
- Note (decision): we deliberately did **not** use `apiKeyHelper` for the pasted
  subscription token. `apiKeyHelper` sends its value as `X-Api-Key` + `Authorization:
  Bearer` *without* the OAuth beta header, so a subscription `sk-ant-oat01-` token likely
  won't authenticate through it. The documented `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` env var is the
  reliable mechanism and is what we ship. Revisit only if Anthropic documents
  `apiKeyHelper` support for OAuth tokens.
- Refs: `src/services/provision.ts` (`buildProvisionCommand`, `captureClaudeCreds`),
  `src/app/(app)/claude-login.tsx`.

### 2. Add a "Re-provision this sprite" action
Credentials are written once per sprite (guarded by `~/.config/.sprite_provisioned`).
Already-provisioned sprites keep stale credentials after a token rotation or a new
captured login — only newly created sprites pick up the latest.

- Add an action (sprite screen or settings) that clears the marker + the credential
  files and re-runs `provisionSprite`, so a rotated token / replaced login propagates to
  an existing sprite.
- Refs: `src/services/provision.ts` (`ensureProvisioned`, `MARKER`, `provisionSprite`).

1	# Chat transport architecture (Claude & Codex)
2	
3	Status: design notes + decisions, updated after keeping the legacy Codex exec
4	provider side-by-side with the first Codex app-server provider. Captures the
5	analysis of how chat turns are transported to/from the agent CLIs inside a
6	sprite, the current model, and the two persistent-session designs we considered.
7	Companion to
8	[`codex-app-server-estimate.md`](./codex-app-server-estimate.md).
9	
10	---
11	
12	## 1. Current model — one-shot exec + resumable provider threads
13	
14	Each chat turn spawns a **fresh process** over the Exec WebSocket and streams its
15	stdout NDJSON back:
16	
17	- Transport: `api.streamExec(sprite, ['bash','-c', cmd], onEvent, signal, opts)`
18	  → `WSS /v1/sprites/{name}/exec` (`src/services/api.ts`).
19	- Claude: `claude -p --verbose --output-format stream-json --dangerously-skip-permissions [--resume <id>] <prompt>`
20	- Codex: provider-level split:
21	  - `Codex`: legacy/fallback `codex exec --json` / `codex exec resume --json`,
22	    parsed through the same `CodexStreamParser`.
23	  - `Codex Server`: `codex app-server --stdio`; the app writes JSON-RPC
24	    requests to stdin (`initialize` → `thread/start` or `thread/resume` →
25	    `turn/start`) and parses app-server notifications from stdout.
26	- Continuity across turns is via **session id resume**, not a live process:
27	  `claude --resume <session_id>` / `thread/resume <thread_id>`. The id comes
28	  from the first `system` / `thread/started` event and is persisted
29	  (`claudeSessionIdRef` / `codexSessionIdRef` in `src/hooks/useChat.ts`).
30	- The process is kept alive *during* a turn by `withSpriteTaskHeartbeat`
31	  (sprite task API `expire 5m`, re-put every 60s; plus a dot every 20s to keep
32	  the stream warm) and `max_run_after_disconnect`, so the app can detach/attach
33	  to an **in-flight** turn (`attachSessionId`).
34	
35	**Why exec and not the Services API** (see the comment at
36	`src/services/api.ts` ~L427): services are *supervised* — the sprite service
37	manager may **restart** a crashed/finished service, which, with the prompt baked
38	into the service `cmd`, **replays the same prompt into `claude --resume`**. Exec
39	sessions never auto-restart and `max_run_after_disconnect` makes disconnect
40	behavior explicit. The legacy service-per-turn chat path is what
41	`cleanupLegacyChatServices` (`wisp-claude-*` / `wisp-codex-*` / `wisp-exec-*`)
42	tears down.
43	
44	### Limits of the current model
45	- **Codex app-server process is still cold per turn.** We get live deltas, but
46	  still pay process startup and thread resume on each turn. That is intentional:
47	  it matches sprite suspend/resume behavior and avoids warm daemon lifecycle.
48	- **Cold start every turn.** `resume` re-launches the process and reloads the
49	  thread from disk each turn.
50	- **Durability gap after a turn ends.** The heartbeat keeps the process alive
51	  *while a turn runs*, but a one-shot turn's process **exits when the turn
52	  completes**. If the app was closed and the turn finished meanwhile, there's no
53	  live stream to reattach to — only locally-persisted messages remain. Claude
54	  recovers via on-disk session files (`syncClaudeTranscript`); Codex had no
55	  equivalent until `syncCodexTranscript` (§6).
56	
57	---
58	
59	## 2. Two independent axes — don't conflate streaming with warmth
60	
61	Everything below stays on the **Exec API** (the app is already exec-based — see
62	§1). The earlier framing of "the ideal architecture = a persistent warm process"
63	was wrong: it bundled two *independent* decisions. Separate them:
64	
65	- **Axis A — process lifetime:** *ephemeral* (a fresh process per turn, cold) vs
66	  *persistent* (one process kept alive across turns, warm).
67	- **Axis B — how a turn is delivered & streamed:** *argv + whole-message*
68	  (`claude -p <prompt>`, legacy `codex exec --json`) vs *stdin + streamed
69	  events* (`claude --input-format stream-json`, `codex app-server --stdio`).
70	
71	> **Sprite reality check.** A sprite suspends when idle — that is the point
72	> (don't burn resources when nobody's looking). Keeping a process *warm for
73	> hours* fights the platform: you'd have to actively prevent suspension (the
74	> heartbeat task even expires at 5m). For the real usage pattern — *write, leave
75	> for hours, come back* — **cold is the correct default.** So **Axis A should
76	> stay ephemeral.** Warm (§2.4) is a niche optimization, not the goal.
77	
78	The useful insight is that **Axis B is independent of Axis A**: you can stream a
79	turn token-by-token while still being *cold per turn*. Streaming is a property of
80	one turn's output format, not of process persistence.
81	
82	### 2.1 The wire protocol (implemented for reads and stdin writes)
83	The Exec WebSocket is **bidirectional**. Binary frames are
84	`[streamId: 1 byte][payload]` (`src/services/api.ts`, `handleBinaryMessage`):
85	
86	| streamId | direction | meaning                |
87	|----------|-----------|------------------------|
88	| `0`      | **client → process** | **stdin** (to write)   |
89	| `1`      | process → client | stdout                 |
90	| `2`      | process → client | stderr                 |
91	| `3`      | process → client | exit (payload = code)  |
92	
93	`StreamExecOptions` exposes `stdin?: boolean` and `onStdinReady`. The writer
94	sends `Uint8Array([0x00, ...utf8(payload)])` frames into the running process.
95	
96	### 2.2 Where each provider stands on streaming (cold, per turn)
97	
98	| | cold per-turn, streams? | to make it stream |
99	|---|---|---|
100	| **Claude** | ✅ already (`-p --output-format stream-json` emits deltas) | nothing — current code already gets this |
101	| **Codex** | ❌ legacy `codex exec --json` returns the final assistant message as a whole | choose the `Codex Server` provider |
102	| **Codex Server** | ✅ via app-server (`item/agentMessage/delta`, reasoning deltas) | spawn `codex app-server --stdio`, push one turn to stdin, stream events, then terminate |
103	
104	So **Codex Server can stream cold** through `codex app-server --stdio`. The
105	streaming fix was *not* warmth — it was adding the app-server provider, still
106	launched **one process per turn**. The legacy `Codex` provider remains
107	available side-by-side as a fallback.
108	
109	### 2.3 Implemented target — *cold-per-turn `codex app-server --stdio` streaming*
110	
111	This keeps Axis A = ephemeral (sprite-friendly) and only moves Codex along
112	Axis B when the `Codex Server` provider is selected:
113	
114	1. Per Codex turn, spawn `codex app-server --stdio` over Exec with `stdin: true`
115	   (no warm keep-alive beyond the in-flight turn — the existing heartbeat covers
116	   "alive while the turn runs").
117	2. Write JSON-RPC to stdin: `initialize`, `initialized`, `thread/start` or
118	   `thread/resume`, then `turn/start`, all `0x00`-framed at the Exec layer.
119	3. Stream app-server notifications back on stdout through `CodexStreamParser`.
120	   It now understands both legacy `codex exec --json` events and app-server
121	   methods such as `item/agentMessage/delta`, `item/started`,
122	   `item/completed`, `turn/plan/updated`, and `turn/completed`.
123	4. On `turn/completed`, kill the app-server exec session. Next turn (possibly
124	   hours later) = a fresh cold spawn that resumes the thread from disk.
125	
126	Cost: one stdin write-path in `streamExec`, `src/services/codex-app-server.ts`,
127	and one extra `AgentProvider` value so the legacy `Codex` path stays available.
128	Cold start is paid once per turn — same tradeoff as legacy `codex exec resume`.
129	**No warm process, no service.**
130	
131	When is this even worth doing? Only if Codex's "tools stream in, then the whole
132	answer appears at once at the end" actually bothers you. If not, the current
133	legacy `codex exec --json` path (plus the §6 transcript sync and the parity
134	fixes) remains useful as a fallback design; the app exposes both Codex paths as
135	separate provider options.
136	
137	### 2.4 Niche only — persistent/warm session
138	
139	Keeping one process alive across turns (fed via stdin, reattached via
140	`WSS .../exec/{session_id}`) removes per-turn cold start *and* gives streaming.
141	But it only pays off for a **tight multi-turn burst inside one active sitting**,
142	where the sprite is awake anyway and cold-start latency between rapid replies is
143	the bottleneck. For "leave for hours" it's the wrong fit (see the reality check
144	above) and is **not recommended as the default**. Mechanics, if ever needed:
145	start idle (no baked prompt) with a large `max_run_after_disconnect`; respawn on
146	death with `--resume <id>` (safe — nothing to replay since no prompt is baked
147	in); discover live sessions via `listExecSessions`.
148	
149	### 2.5 Code touchpoints (for §2.3)
150	- `api.ts`: `ExecStdinWriter` + `onStdinReady`, framed as stream id `0`.
151	- `src/services/codex-app-server.ts`: app-server JSON-RPC state machine
152	  (`initialize` → thread start/resume → turn start).
153	- `src/models/codex-events.ts`: app-server notification mapping to existing
154	  `CodexStreamEvent`.
155	- `useChat.ts`: Codex turns route through either the app-server driver or the
156	  legacy `codex exec --json` command based on `AgentProvider`.
157	- `models/chat.ts`, `settings.tsx`, `ChatInputBar.tsx`, `NewSessionSheet.tsx`,
158	  and `storage.ts`: `Codex` and `Codex Server` are exposed side-by-side as
159	  provider options.
160	
161	### 2.6 Risks / open items
162	- The implemented schema was generated from `codex-cli 0.137.0`
163	  (`codex app-server generate-ts --experimental`). It should be rechecked when
164	  the installed Codex CLI changes.
165	- Claude `--input-format stream-json` input message shape (only relevant if the
166	  niche warm path in §2.4 is ever pursued).
167	- Live sprite verification is still needed for the real hosted Exec WebSocket,
168	  although local CLI stdio framing was verified as newline-delimited JSON-RPC.
169	
170	### 2.7 Legacy exec vs app-server exec — what actually changes
171	
172	Both are the **same Exec WebSocket transport**; the delta is small and Codex-only.
173	
174	| | Legacy Codex exec | App-server exec (§2.3) |
175	|---|---|---|
176	| Process lifetime | ephemeral, cold per turn | **same** — ephemeral, cold per turn |
177	| Sprite suspends when idle | yes (desired) | **same** (desired) |
178	| Continuity | `--resume` / `exec resume <id>` | **same** (resume by id) |
179	| Claude streaming | ✅ already | ✅ unchanged |
180	| Codex per-turn binary | legacy `codex exec --json` | **`codex app-server --stdio`** |
181	| Codex prompt delivery | argv (`<prompt>` in bash line) | **stdin frame** (`0x00`+payload) |
182	| Codex output | whole `agent_message` at end | **streamed** reasoning/text deltas |
183	| `streamExec` direction | read-only | **read + write (stdin)** |
184	| Durability after idle | §6 transcript sync | **same** (§6) |
185	| Services / FIFO / warm keep-alive | none | **none** |
186	
187	Net: the *only* moving parts are (a) teach `streamExec` to write a stdin frame
188	and (b) drive Codex turns through app-server instead of `codex exec`. Process
189	model, cold-start behavior, resume, and durability remain the same.
190	
191	---
192	
193	## 3. Alternative A — FIFO injection
194	
195	If, for some reason, we run the agent as a process whose stdin we cannot address
196	directly over WS, inject prompts through a named pipe inside the sprite:
197	
198	```sh
199	mkfifo /tmp/chat.in
200	# keep the FIFO open so per-message writers don't EOF the reader:
201	sleep infinity > /tmp/chat.in &
202	claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json < /tmp/chat.in
203	```
204	
205	Each prompt is a tiny **separate exec**: `printf '%s\n' "$JSON" > /tmp/chat.in`.
206	Output still streams on the agent process's stdout (capture via exec attach or,
207	if run as a service, the service log buffer).
208	
209	**Gotchas:** FIFO EOF handling (must hold a writer fd open, hence the
210	`sleep infinity > fifo`); one FIFO per session; cleanup of the pipe. Strictly
211	worse than §2.3 because it needs a side process and an extra exec per turn — keep
212	it only as a fallback.
213	
214	---
215	
216	## 4. Alternative B — per-conversation service **without a startup prompt**
217	
218	> Documented in depth because this is a likely implementation target. The core
219	> idea fixes the exact reason we left the Services API: **don't bake the prompt
220	> into the service `cmd`.** A restart then just yields a fresh idle process that
221	> does nothing until a prompt is delivered — no replay.
222	
223	### 4.1 Shape
224	- **One service per chat conversation** (not per turn). Name it deterministically
225	  from the chat id, e.g. `wisp-agent-<chatId>`, so reopening the chat finds it
226	  via `listServices` / `getServiceStatus`.
227	- Service `cmd` starts the agent in **persistent, prompt-less stdin mode**:
228	  - Claude: `claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --dangerously-skip-permissions --resume <id?> --model <m>`
229	  - Codex: `codex app-server --stdio`
230	  - **No prompt argument anywhere.** The process boots, opens stdin, and idles.
231	- Register via `PUT /v1/sprites/{name}/services/{service}` with
232	  `ServiceRequest { cmd, args?, needs?, http_port? }` (see `streamService`).
233	
234	### 4.2 Delivering prompts (input channel)
235	The service is supervised; we still need a way *in*. Options, best first:
236	1. **FIFO** the service reads from (as §3): service `cmd` reads `< /tmp/<svc>.in`;
237	   a prompt is a small exec `printf … > /tmp/<svc>.in`. Survives restarts if the
238	   FIFO is recreated on boot (wrap the service cmd in a small shell that
239	   `mkfifo -p` + holds it open).
240	2. **Local HTTP wrapper**: service runs a tiny daemon owning the agent child and
241	   exposing `POST /turn` on `http_port`; reach it via the sprite TCP proxy
242	   (`WSS /v1/sprites/{name}/proxy`). More moving parts, but clean request/response
243	   and back-pressure.
244	3. **Watched file/queue**: prompt written via `PUT /filesystem/files`; a wrapper
245	   tails it. Simplest to write, least elegant (polling).
246	
247	### 4.3 Reading output (durability win)
248	Read the service's stdout from the **durable log buffer**:
249	`GET /v1/sprites/{name}/services/{service}/logs?lines=<n>&duration=<follow>`
250	(`streamServiceLogs`). This is the big advantage over exec: the buffer
251	**survives the app being killed and survives turns completing**, so reopening a
252	chat = `streamServiceLogs(lines=all)` replayed through the existing parser →
253	full state rebuilt. (Buffer may be ring-capped for very long sessions; treat the
254	agent's own on-disk transcript — §6 — as the ultimate source of truth.)
255	
256	### 4.4 Restart semantics — why "no startup prompt" matters
257	- A supervised restart of a **prompt-less** service = a fresh idle reader. **No
258	  prompt is replayed** (the historical failure mode).
259	- The cost: a restart drops the warm in-memory thread. On (re)start, pass
260	  `--resume <id>` (Claude) / resume the thread (`thread/resume`) so context is
261	  reloaded from disk. Persist the id locally and in the service args.
262	- Concurrency: one service per chat ⇒ stable name avoids collisions; multiple
263	  open chats ⇒ multiple services. Garbage-collect idle/stale services
264	  (extend `cleanupLegacyChatServices` with the new prefix + an age/last-activity
265	  check).
266	
267	### 4.5 Lifecycle checklist (for implementation)
268	- [ ] Create-or-attach: `getServiceStatus` → if missing, `streamService`/PUT to
269	      create with prompt-less cmd + resume id.
270	- [ ] Input channel chosen (FIFO recommended for a first cut).
271	- [ ] Output via `streamServiceLogs` (`lines` backfill on open, `duration` follow).
272	- [ ] Map events through existing `ClaudeStreamParser` / `CodexStreamParser`.
273	- [ ] Resume id threaded into service args; re-create on restart without replay.
274	- [ ] Stop/cleanup: `deleteService` on explicit chat close; periodic GC of stale
275	      `wisp-agent-*` services.
276	- [ ] Concurrency cap / eviction policy for many open chats.
277	
278	### 4.6 Pros / cons vs §2.3
279	- **Pro:** supervised auto-restart (resilience) for free; durable log buffer for
280	  replay; doesn't need the §2.5 stdin-writer change to `streamExec`.
281	- **Con:** brings back service lifecycle (naming, GC) we deliberately shed; still
282	  needs a side input channel (FIFO/HTTP); restart can interrupt an in-flight turn
283	  mid-way (mitigate by resume + idempotent turn handling).
284	
285	---
286	
287	## 5. Comparison
288	
289	| Property | legacy exec + resume | **§2.3 cold-per-turn app-server** (implemented) | §2.4 persistent/warm (niche) | §4 per-chat service (niche) |
290	|---|---|---|---|---|
291	| API | Exec | Exec | Exec | Services |
292	| Process lifetime | ephemeral (cold) | **ephemeral (cold)** | persistent (warm) | persistent (supervised) |
293	| Sprite-friendly (suspends idle) | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ fights suspend | ❌ fights suspend |
294	| Codex streaming | ❌ whole message | ✅ (`codex app-server --stdio`) | ✅ | ✅ |
295	| Cold start / turn | yes | yes (accepted) | no | no |
296	| Follow-ups | ✅ via resume | ✅ via resume + stdin | ✅ via stdin | ✅ via input channel |
297	| Durability after idle | ✅ §6 transcript sync | ✅ §6 transcript sync | ✅ §6 (+ live if alive) | ✅ durable log buffer |
298	| Prompt-replay risk | none | none | none | none (no baked prompt) |
299	| Extra machinery | none | stdin writer + app-server driver | + keep-alive/respawn | service GC + input channel |
300	| Lifecycle cost | lowest | low | medium | medium-high |
301	
302	**Recommendation:** for the real "write → leave → come back" pattern, stay
303	**ephemeral/cold** (the sprite model wants this). The only worthwhile upgrade is
304	**§2.3 — route Codex turns through `codex app-server --stdio` for live
305	streaming**, still one cold process per turn. **§2.4 (warm)** and **§4
306	(service)** are niche — justified only by a tight multi-turn burst in one active
307	sitting, and both work against sprite suspension. Durability after idle is
308	already handled cold by §6 for every option, so it is not a reason to go warm.
309	
310	---
311	
312	## 6. Durability today — `syncCodexTranscript` (implemented)
313	
314	Independent of §2/§4, Codex now has the same on-disk transcript recovery Claude
315	has. Codex CLI writes a **rollout** per thread:
316	`~/.codex/sessions/<YYYY>/<MM>/<DD>/rollout-<ts>-<thread_id>.jsonl`. The
317	`<thread_id>` is the same UUID we store as `codexSessionId` (from
318	`thread.started`). See `src/services/codex-sessions.ts`.
319	
320	Rollout line envelope: `{type, payload, timestamp}` where `type` ∈
321	`session_meta | response_item | event_msg | turn_context | compacted`. Mapping to
322	the app's `ChatMessage[]`:
323	
324	| Source line | → rendered as |
325	|---|---|
326	| `event_msg/user_message` (`.message`) | user bubble (clean human prompt) |
327	| `event_msg/agent_message` (`.message`) | assistant text (visible narration) |
328	| `response_item/function_call` (`exec_command`, args `.cmd`) | `Bash` tool card, linked by `call_id` |
329	| `response_item/function_call_output` (`.output`) | tool result |
330	| `response_item/custom_tool_call` (`apply_patch`, `.input`) | `Edit` tool card |
331	| `response_item/custom_tool_call_output` | tool result |
332	| `response_item/web_search_call` (`.action.query`) | `WebSearch` tool card |
333	| `response_item/reasoning` | **skipped** — `summary: []`, only `encrypted_content` (no plaintext) |
334	| `response_item/message` (developer/user/assistant) | skipped — covered by `event_msg` equivalents; developer/AGENTS.md preamble is noise |
335	| `event_msg/{token_count,task_started,task_complete,patch_apply_end,web_search_end}` | skipped (redundant/usage) |
336	
337	Like Claude, this is read sprite-side via a `node` script behind sentinel
338	markers so we transfer a few KB, not full transcripts, and it survives app
339	close / reinstall.

# Chat transport architecture (Claude & Codex)

Status: design notes + decisions, updated after keeping the legacy Codex exec
provider side-by-side with the first Codex app-server provider. Captures the
analysis of how chat turns are transported to/from the agent CLIs inside a
sprite, the current model, and the two persistent-session designs we considered.
Companion to
[`codex-app-server-estimate.md`](./codex-app-server-estimate.md).

---

## 1. Current model — one-shot exec + resumable provider threads

Each chat turn spawns a **fresh process** over the Exec WebSocket and streams its
stdout NDJSON back:

- Transport: `api.streamExec(sprite, ['bash','-c', cmd], onEvent, signal, opts)`
  → `WSS /v1/sprites/{name}/exec` (`src/services/api.ts`).
- Claude: `claude -p --verbose --output-format stream-json --dangerously-skip-permissions [--resume <id>] <prompt>`
- Codex: provider-level split:
  - `Codex`: legacy/fallback `codex exec --json` / `codex exec resume --json`,
    parsed through the same `CodexStreamParser`.
  - `Codex Server`: `codex app-server --stdio`; the app writes JSON-RPC
    requests to stdin (`initialize` → `thread/start` or `thread/resume` →
    `turn/start`) and parses app-server notifications from stdout.
- Continuity across turns is via **session id resume**, not a live process:
  `claude --resume <session_id>` / `thread/resume <thread_id>`. The id comes
  from the first `system` / `thread/started` event and is persisted
  (`claudeSessionIdRef` / `codexSessionIdRef` in `src/hooks/useChat.ts`).
- The process is kept alive *during* a turn by `withSpriteTaskHeartbeat`
  (sprite task API `expire 5m`, re-put every 60s; plus a dot every 20s to keep
  the stream warm) and `max_run_after_disconnect`, so the app can detach/attach
  to an **in-flight** turn (`attachSessionId`).

**Why exec and not the Services API** (see the comment at
`src/services/api.ts` ~L427): services are *supervised* — the sprite service
manager may **restart** a crashed/finished service, which, with the prompt baked
into the service `cmd`, **replays the same prompt into `claude --resume`**. Exec
sessions never auto-restart and `max_run_after_disconnect` makes disconnect
behavior explicit. The legacy service-per-turn chat path is what
`cleanupLegacyChatServices` (`wisp-claude-*` / `wisp-codex-*` / `wisp-exec-*`)
tears down.

### Limits of the current model
- **Codex app-server process is still cold per turn.** We get live deltas, but
  still pay process startup and thread resume on each turn. That is intentional:
  it matches sprite suspend/resume behavior and avoids warm daemon lifecycle.
- **Cold start every turn.** `resume` re-launches the process and reloads the
  thread from disk each turn.
- **Durability gap after a turn ends.** The heartbeat keeps the process alive
  *while a turn runs*, but a one-shot turn's process **exits when the turn
  completes**. If the app was closed and the turn finished meanwhile, there's no
  live stream to reattach to — only locally-persisted messages remain. Claude
  recovers via on-disk session files (`syncClaudeTranscript`); Codex had no
  equivalent until `syncCodexTranscript` (§6).

---

## 2. Two independent axes — don't conflate streaming with warmth

Everything below stays on the **Exec API** (the app is already exec-based — see
§1). The earlier framing of "the ideal architecture = a persistent warm process"
was wrong: it bundled two *independent* decisions. Separate them:

- **Axis A — process lifetime:** *ephemeral* (a fresh process per turn, cold) vs
  *persistent* (one process kept alive across turns, warm).
- **Axis B — how a turn is delivered & streamed:** *argv + whole-message*
  (`claude -p <prompt>`, legacy `codex exec --json`) vs *stdin + streamed
  events* (`claude --input-format stream-json`, `codex app-server --stdio`).

> **Sprite reality check.** A sprite suspends when idle — that is the point
> (don't burn resources when nobody's looking). Keeping a process *warm for
> hours* fights the platform: you'd have to actively prevent suspension (the
> heartbeat task even expires at 5m). For the real usage pattern — *write, leave
> for hours, come back* — **cold is the correct default.** So **Axis A should
> stay ephemeral.** Warm (§2.4) is a niche optimization, not the goal.

The useful insight is that **Axis B is independent of Axis A**: you can stream a
turn token-by-token while still being *cold per turn*. Streaming is a property of
one turn's output format, not of process persistence.

### 2.1 The wire protocol (implemented for reads and stdin writes)
The Exec WebSocket is **bidirectional**. Binary frames are
`[streamId: 1 byte][payload]` (`src/services/api.ts`, `handleBinaryMessage`):

| streamId | direction | meaning                |
|----------|-----------|------------------------|
| `0`      | **client → process** | **stdin** (to write)   |
| `1`      | process → client | stdout                 |
| `2`      | process → client | stderr                 |
| `3`      | process → client | exit (payload = code)  |

`StreamExecOptions` exposes `stdin?: boolean` and `onStdinReady`. The writer
sends `Uint8Array([0x00, ...utf8(payload)])` frames into the running process.

### 2.2 Where each provider stands on streaming (cold, per turn)

| | cold per-turn, streams? | to make it stream |
|---|---|---|
| **Claude** | ✅ already (`-p --output-format stream-json` emits deltas) | nothing — current code already gets this |
| **Codex** | ❌ legacy `codex exec --json` returns the final assistant message as a whole | choose the `Codex Server` provider |
| **Codex Server** | ✅ via app-server (`item/agentMessage/delta`, reasoning deltas) | spawn `codex app-server --stdio`, push one turn to stdin, stream events, then terminate |

So **Codex Server can stream cold** through `codex app-server --stdio`. The
streaming fix was *not* warmth — it was adding the app-server provider, still
launched **one process per turn**. The legacy `Codex` provider remains
available side-by-side as a fallback.

### 2.3 Implemented target — *cold-per-turn `codex app-server --stdio` streaming*

This keeps Axis A = ephemeral (sprite-friendly) and only moves Codex along
Axis B when the `Codex Server` provider is selected:

1. Per Codex turn, spawn `codex app-server --stdio` over Exec with `stdin: true`
   (no warm keep-alive beyond the in-flight turn — the existing heartbeat covers
   "alive while the turn runs").
2. Write JSON-RPC to stdin: `initialize`, `initialized`, `thread/start` or
   `thread/resume`, then `turn/start`, all `0x00`-framed at the Exec layer.
3. Stream app-server notifications back on stdout through `CodexStreamParser`.
   It now understands both legacy `codex exec --json` events and app-server
   methods such as `item/agentMessage/delta`, `item/started`,
   `item/completed`, `turn/plan/updated`, and `turn/completed`.
4. On `turn/completed`, kill the app-server exec session. Next turn (possibly
   hours later) = a fresh cold spawn that resumes the thread from disk.

Cost: one stdin write-path in `streamExec`, `src/services/codex-app-server.ts`,
and one extra `AgentProvider` value so the legacy `Codex` path stays available.
Cold start is paid once per turn — same tradeoff as legacy `codex exec resume`.
**No warm process, no service.**

When is this even worth doing? Only if Codex's "tools stream in, then the whole
answer appears at once at the end" actually bothers you. If not, the current
legacy `codex exec --json` path (plus the §6 transcript sync and the parity
fixes) remains useful as a fallback design; the app exposes both Codex paths as
separate provider options.

### 2.4 Niche only — persistent/warm session

Keeping one process alive across turns (fed via stdin, reattached via
`WSS .../exec/{session_id}`) removes per-turn cold start *and* gives streaming.
But it only pays off for a **tight multi-turn burst inside one active sitting**,
where the sprite is awake anyway and cold-start latency between rapid replies is
the bottleneck. For "leave for hours" it's the wrong fit (see the reality check
above) and is **not recommended as the default**. Mechanics, if ever needed:
start idle (no baked prompt) with a large `max_run_after_disconnect`; respawn on
death with `--resume <id>` (safe — nothing to replay since no prompt is baked
in); discover live sessions via `listExecSessions`.

### 2.5 Code touchpoints (for §2.3)
- `api.ts`: `ExecStdinWriter` + `onStdinReady`, framed as stream id `0`.
- `src/services/codex-app-server.ts`: app-server JSON-RPC state machine
  (`initialize` → thread start/resume → turn start).
- `src/models/codex-events.ts`: app-server notification mapping to existing
  `CodexStreamEvent`.
- `useChat.ts`: Codex turns route through either the app-server driver or the
  legacy `codex exec --json` command based on `AgentProvider`.
- `models/chat.ts`, `settings.tsx`, `ChatInputBar.tsx`, `NewSessionSheet.tsx`,
  and `storage.ts`: `Codex` and `Codex Server` are exposed side-by-side as
  provider options.

### 2.6 Risks / open items
- The implemented schema was generated from `codex-cli 0.137.0`
  (`codex app-server generate-ts --experimental`). It should be rechecked when
  the installed Codex CLI changes.
- Claude `--input-format stream-json` input message shape (only relevant if the
  niche warm path in §2.4 is ever pursued).
- Live sprite verification is still needed for the real hosted Exec WebSocket,
  although local CLI stdio framing was verified as newline-delimited JSON-RPC.

### 2.7 Legacy exec vs app-server exec — what actually changes

Both are the **same Exec WebSocket transport**; the delta is small and Codex-only.

| | Legacy Codex exec | App-server exec (§2.3) |
|---|---|---|
| Process lifetime | ephemeral, cold per turn | **same** — ephemeral, cold per turn |
| Sprite suspends when idle | yes (desired) | **same** (desired) |
| Continuity | `--resume` / `exec resume <id>` | **same** (resume by id) |
| Claude streaming | ✅ already | ✅ unchanged |
| Codex per-turn binary | legacy `codex exec --json` | **`codex app-server --stdio`** |
| Codex prompt delivery | argv (`<prompt>` in bash line) | **stdin frame** (`0x00`+payload) |
| Codex output | whole `agent_message` at end | **streamed** reasoning/text deltas |
| `streamExec` direction | read-only | **read + write (stdin)** |
| Durability after idle | §6 transcript sync | **same** (§6) |
| Services / FIFO / warm keep-alive | none | **none** |

Net: the *only* moving parts are (a) teach `streamExec` to write a stdin frame
and (b) drive Codex turns through app-server instead of `codex exec`. Process
model, cold-start behavior, resume, and durability remain the same.

---

## 3. Alternative A — FIFO injection

If, for some reason, we run the agent as a process whose stdin we cannot address
directly over WS, inject prompts through a named pipe inside the sprite:

```sh
mkfifo /tmp/chat.in
# keep the FIFO open so per-message writers don't EOF the reader:
sleep infinity > /tmp/chat.in &
claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json < /tmp/chat.in
```

Each prompt is a tiny **separate exec**: `printf '%s\n' "$JSON" > /tmp/chat.in`.
Output still streams on the agent process's stdout (capture via exec attach or,
if run as a service, the service log buffer).

**Gotchas:** FIFO EOF handling (must hold a writer fd open, hence the
`sleep infinity > fifo`); one FIFO per session; cleanup of the pipe. Strictly
worse than §2.3 because it needs a side process and an extra exec per turn — keep
it only as a fallback.

---

## 4. Alternative B — per-conversation service **without a startup prompt**

> Documented in depth because this is a likely implementation target. The core
> idea fixes the exact reason we left the Services API: **don't bake the prompt
> into the service `cmd`.** A restart then just yields a fresh idle process that
> does nothing until a prompt is delivered — no replay.

### 4.1 Shape
- **One service per chat conversation** (not per turn). Name it deterministically
  from the chat id, e.g. `wisp-agent-<chatId>`, so reopening the chat finds it
  via `listServices` / `getServiceStatus`.
- Service `cmd` starts the agent in **persistent, prompt-less stdin mode**:
  - Claude: `claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --dangerously-skip-permissions --resume <id?> --model <m>`
  - Codex: `codex app-server --stdio`
  - **No prompt argument anywhere.** The process boots, opens stdin, and idles.
- Register via `PUT /v1/sprites/{name}/services/{service}` with
  `ServiceRequest { cmd, args?, needs?, http_port? }` (see `streamService`).

### 4.2 Delivering prompts (input channel)
The service is supervised; we still need a way *in*. Options, best first:
1. **FIFO** the service reads from (as §3): service `cmd` reads `< /tmp/<svc>.in`;
   a prompt is a small exec `printf … > /tmp/<svc>.in`. Survives restarts if the
   FIFO is recreated on boot (wrap the service cmd in a small shell that
   `mkfifo -p` + holds it open).
2. **Local HTTP wrapper**: service runs a tiny daemon owning the agent child and
   exposing `POST /turn` on `http_port`; reach it via the sprite TCP proxy
   (`WSS /v1/sprites/{name}/proxy`). More moving parts, but clean request/response
   and back-pressure.
3. **Watched file/queue**: prompt written via `PUT /filesystem/files`; a wrapper
   tails it. Simplest to write, least elegant (polling).

### 4.3 Reading output (durability win)
Read the service's stdout from the **durable log buffer**:
`GET /v1/sprites/{name}/services/{service}/logs?lines=<n>&duration=<follow>`
(`streamServiceLogs`). This is the big advantage over exec: the buffer
**survives the app being killed and survives turns completing**, so reopening a
chat = `streamServiceLogs(lines=all)` replayed through the existing parser →
full state rebuilt. (Buffer may be ring-capped for very long sessions; treat the
agent's own on-disk transcript — §6 — as the ultimate source of truth.)

### 4.4 Restart semantics — why "no startup prompt" matters
- A supervised restart of a **prompt-less** service = a fresh idle reader. **No
  prompt is replayed** (the historical failure mode).
- The cost: a restart drops the warm in-memory thread. On (re)start, pass
  `--resume <id>` (Claude) / resume the thread (`thread/resume`) so context is
  reloaded from disk. Persist the id locally and in the service args.
- Concurrency: one service per chat ⇒ stable name avoids collisions; multiple
  open chats ⇒ multiple services. Garbage-collect idle/stale services
  (extend `cleanupLegacyChatServices` with the new prefix + an age/last-activity
  check).

### 4.5 Lifecycle checklist (for implementation)
- [ ] Create-or-attach: `getServiceStatus` → if missing, `streamService`/PUT to
      create with prompt-less cmd + resume id.
- [ ] Input channel chosen (FIFO recommended for a first cut).
- [ ] Output via `streamServiceLogs` (`lines` backfill on open, `duration` follow).
- [ ] Map events through existing `ClaudeStreamParser` / `CodexStreamParser`.
- [ ] Resume id threaded into service args; re-create on restart without replay.
- [ ] Stop/cleanup: `deleteService` on explicit chat close; periodic GC of stale
      `wisp-agent-*` services.
- [ ] Concurrency cap / eviction policy for many open chats.

### 4.6 Pros / cons vs §2.3
- **Pro:** supervised auto-restart (resilience) for free; durable log buffer for
  replay; doesn't need the §2.5 stdin-writer change to `streamExec`.
- **Con:** brings back service lifecycle (naming, GC) we deliberately shed; still
  needs a side input channel (FIFO/HTTP); restart can interrupt an in-flight turn
  mid-way (mitigate by resume + idempotent turn handling).

---

## 5. Comparison

| Property | legacy exec + resume | **§2.3 cold-per-turn app-server** (implemented) | §2.4 persistent/warm (niche) | §4 per-chat service (niche) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| API | Exec | Exec | Exec | Services |
| Process lifetime | ephemeral (cold) | **ephemeral (cold)** | persistent (warm) | persistent (supervised) |
| Sprite-friendly (suspends idle) | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ fights suspend | ❌ fights suspend |
| Codex streaming | ❌ whole message | ✅ (`codex app-server --stdio`) | ✅ | ✅ |
| Cold start / turn | yes | yes (accepted) | no | no |
| Follow-ups | ✅ via resume | ✅ via resume + stdin | ✅ via stdin | ✅ via input channel |
| Durability after idle | ✅ §6 transcript sync | ✅ §6 transcript sync | ✅ §6 (+ live if alive) | ✅ durable log buffer |
| Prompt-replay risk | none | none | none | none (no baked prompt) |
| Extra machinery | none | stdin writer + app-server driver | + keep-alive/respawn | service GC + input channel |
| Lifecycle cost | lowest | low | medium | medium-high |

**Recommendation:** for the real "write → leave → come back" pattern, stay
**ephemeral/cold** (the sprite model wants this). The only worthwhile upgrade is
**§2.3 — route Codex turns through `codex app-server --stdio` for live
streaming**, still one cold process per turn. **§2.4 (warm)** and **§4
(service)** are niche — justified only by a tight multi-turn burst in one active
sitting, and both work against sprite suspension. Durability after idle is
already handled cold by §6 for every option, so it is not a reason to go warm.

---

## 6. Durability today — `syncCodexTranscript` (implemented)

Independent of §2/§4, Codex now has the same on-disk transcript recovery Claude
has. Codex CLI writes a **rollout** per thread:
`~/.codex/sessions/<YYYY>/<MM>/<DD>/rollout-<ts>-<thread_id>.jsonl`. The
`<thread_id>` is the same UUID we store as `codexSessionId` (from
`thread.started`). See `src/services/codex-sessions.ts`.

Rollout line envelope: `{type, payload, timestamp}` where `type` ∈
`session_meta | response_item | event_msg | turn_context | compacted`. Mapping to
the app's `ChatMessage[]`:

| Source line | → rendered as |
|---|---|
| `event_msg/user_message` (`.message`) | user bubble (clean human prompt) |
| `event_msg/agent_message` (`.message`) | assistant text (visible narration) |
| `response_item/function_call` (`exec_command`, args `.cmd`) | `Bash` tool card, linked by `call_id` |
| `response_item/function_call_output` (`.output`) | tool result |
| `response_item/custom_tool_call` (`apply_patch`, `.input`) | `Edit` tool card |
| `response_item/custom_tool_call_output` | tool result |
| `response_item/web_search_call` (`.action.query`) | `WebSearch` tool card |
| `response_item/reasoning` | **skipped** — `summary: []`, only `encrypted_content` (no plaintext) |
| `response_item/message` (developer/user/assistant) | skipped — covered by `event_msg` equivalents; developer/AGENTS.md preamble is noise |
| `event_msg/{token_count,task_started,task_complete,patch_apply_end,web_search_end}` | skipped (redundant/usage) |

Like Claude, this is read sprite-side via a `node` script behind sentinel
markers so we transfer a few KB, not full transcripts, and it survives app
close / reinstall.
